hints: Focus on what is left behind as a solid after heating, as percentage mass loss depends on how much escapes as gas or liquid.
Calculate the molar masses, $M_r$ of $\text{Pb(NO}_3)_2$ is about 331 and $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$ is 80, and work out the mass lost per mole from each equation.
Remember acidic gases like $\text{NO}_2$ are absorbed by $\text{NaOH(aq)}$, while $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{N}_2$ pass straight through to be collected.
walkthrough:
**Compare percentage mass loss**

Think of mass loss as everything that leaves the solid. For lead nitrate a solid residue of $\text{PbO}$ stays behind, but for ammonium nitrate there is no solid residue at all.

$$2\text{Pb(NO}_3)_2(s) \rightarrow 2\text{PbO(s)} + 4\text{NO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$$
$$2\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3(s) \rightarrow 2\text{N}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) + 4\text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$$

**Check the numbers for 1 mole**

For 1 mol $\text{Pb(NO}_3)_2$ (about 331 g), you get 1 mol $\text{PbO}$ (about 223 g) left. Mass lost is about 108 g, so percentage loss is about 32.6%.

$$\text{% loss (Pb)} = \frac{331 - 223}{331} \times 100 \approx 32.6\%$$
For 1 mol $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$ (80 g), no solid remains, so all 80 g is lost. That is 100% loss, clearly greater.

**Decide which gases survive NaOH**

$\text{NO}_2$ is acidic and reacts with $\text{NaOH(aq)}$, so it is removed. $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ are neutral and do not react, so they are collected. $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is given as liquid, so it does not count as collected gas.

**Count collected gas per mole of nitrate**

From 1 mol $\text{Pb(NO}_3)_2$: 2 mol $\text{NO}_2$ is absorbed, only 0.5 mol $\text{O}_2$ is collected.

$$\text{collected (Pb)} = 0.5 \text{ mol}$$
From 1 mol $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$: 1 mol $\text{N}_2$ + 0.5 mol $\text{O}_2$ both pass through.

$$\text{collected (NH}_4\text{NO}_3) = 1.0 + 0.5 = 1.5 \text{ mol}$$
So $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$ gives the greater collected volume and also the greater percentage mass loss.

options.A: Correct. NH4NO3 leaves no solid residue so loses 100% of its mass, more than the ~33% lost by Pb(NO3)2. After NaOH absorption, NH4NO3 gives 1.5 mol of unreacted gas (N2 + O2) per mole, more than the 0.5 mol O2 from Pb(NO3)2.
options.B: Incorrect for the second column. It is tempting to think Pb(NO3)2 gives more gas because its equation shows 2.5 mol of gas per mole, but 2 mol of that is NO2 which is absorbed by NaOH, leaving only 0.5 mol.
options.C: Incorrect for the first column. Pb(NO3)2 seems heavier so the absolute mass lost (108 g) is larger than for NH4NO3 (80 g), but percentage loss is what matters. PbO remains as a heavy solid, so percentage loss is only ~33% versus 100%.
options.D: Incorrect on both counts. This choice ignores that NH4NO3 decomposes completely with no solid left, and ignores that NO2 is removed by NaOH, both of which favour NH4NO3.
